lens: Every identifier the document prints — PMID, PMCID, DOI, GEO series/sample/platform, SRA study, BioProject, Cellosaurus, DepMap, COSMIC-CLP, RIKEN, GenBank/RefSeq accession, GO term, compound code and git commit — resolved against a fetched record rather than recollection, then checked to see whether the record it names actually says what the sentence citing it claims; with species/disease/population provenance asked of every citation (this paper's mechanism was measured on OTHER fusions in OTHER diseases), a retraction and disputed-identity sweep, and an anchoring check of every identifier against the citation-provenance ledger and the producing fetch caches.
_verdict_note: No identifier in this document is fabricated, none is retracted, and every accession-shaped identifier it prints (13 GPL, 2 SRP, 1 PRJNA, CVCL_1238, ACH-001519, 7 GenBank/RefSeq accessions, GO:0031297, RCB0508, COSMIC-CLP 907290) is anchored in one of the four producing fetch artifacts. The four block quotations attributed to the bioRxiv preprint verify VERBATIM against PMC10187251 and all four sit inside the artifact's stored 54 sentences; the Cellosaurus caution is verbatim from the committed record; the Bangerter quotation is verbatim from PubMed's abstract; the gene-set names, sizes and library citations match the cache exactly and all four resource citations are real. The reservations are (1) the sole primary source under the document's self-declared most consequential finding is a paper the document never opened and mischaracterises, (2) a 'what would move the grade' row states as unknown a dataset this repository measured three and a half weeks before the pin, and (3) one reference carries two different years in one document. None overturns a verdict; each changes how much weight a reader can place on a load-bearing sentence.
central_claim: The identifiers hold: nothing fabricated, nothing retracted, nothing unanchored, and every quotation verbatim against the version actually cited. What does not hold is what the document says ABOUT three of its citations — a 'primary source' it never opened and whose subject is a different question in a different population, an SRA deposit called unknown that this repository has already characterised and published a manuscript about, and a journal year that contradicts itself between §2.2 and the Appendix.

p1s.summary: §2.1 calls PMID 34413129 'a primary source' for the Cellosaurus caution that carries the document's self-declared 'most consequential finding' — but that PMID is an SLFN11 pediatric-sarcoma biomarker study that names H-EMC-SS exactly once, in a Materials-and-Methods cell-line provenance list, and never states a per-line fusion result. The document neither opens it nor tells the reader what it is, so a reader cannot weigh the evidence §2 rests on.
p1s.evidence: The identifier resolves and is transcribed correctly: emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_a.cellosaurus.fusion_mentions_verbatim holds the caution byte-for-byte, '(PubMed=34413129)' included, and the sweep records PMID:34413129 as clean. What it resolves TO, fetched from PubMed/PMC: Gartrell J, Mellado-Largarde M, Clay MR, et al., 'SLFN11 is Widely Expressed in Pediatric Sarcoma and Induces Variable Sensitization to Replicative Stress Caused By DNA-Damaging Agents', Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20(11):2151-2165, PMC8571037, doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-21-0089. In its PMC full text (53.5 KB) the string 'H-EMC-SS' occurs ONCE — 'H-EMC-SS (European Collection of Authenticated Cell Cultures, RRID:CVCL_1238)' in the cell-line list — and the words 'myxoid' and 'chondrosarcoma' occur ZERO times. The only methods sentence that could underlie the caution is panel-wide and reports no per-line result: 'Cell lines were authenticated using short tandem repeat analysis via PowerPlex (Promega) and tested for mycoplasma using MycoAlert (Lonza). Translocation status was confirmed using PCR and Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH).' On population provenance the mismatch is explicit: the paper's stated subject is PEDIATRIC sarcoma (220 children), while Cellosaurus records H-EMC-SS as AG 77Y, SX Female — an adult-derived line outside the study's population. ⛔ THIS DOES NOT REFUTE THE CAUTION: the panel-wide PCR/FISH sentence makes a curator-read fusion call plausible, and §2.2's claim is correctly bounded to 'the public record does not support' with an explicit ⛔ list of what is NOT established, so the bounded claim survives. What fails is the characterisation, and it fails in the direction that flatters the finding.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace 'citing a primary source' with what the source is and what it does and does not report — e.g. 'citing Gartrell et al., Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20:2151-2165 (PMID 34413129), a pediatric-sarcoma SLFN11 study that used H-EMC-SS in its panel and states only panel-wide that translocation status was confirmed by PCR and FISH; no per-line fusion result appears in its text.' Any edit that keeps the phrase 'primary source' without naming the paper leaves the reader unable to weigh §2, and any edit that asserts the paper characterised H-EMC-SS reintroduces a claim its retrievable text does not carry.

p1s.summary: §6.3 states that for SRP640302 'the sample sizes and fusion annotation are unknown until it is opened' — this repository opened it on 2026-08-08, three and a half weeks before the pin, and committed both the measurement and the deposit's publication. §6.3 also names SRP445369 under the header 'EMC RNA-seq quantified from raw reads', but that study's own deposited name is a WHOLE-GENOME study, from which no expression matrix can be quantified.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-sra-study.json (_generated_utc 2026-08-08T20:25:51Z): target_sra_study SRP640302, target_bioproject PRJNA1357027, resolved true for both, pairing_check verdict CONSISTENT, transport_gate_passed true, verdict.grade EMC_PUBLIC_CANDIDATE with headline 'an EMC deposit with 12 runs over 12 samples is public and downloadable; library strategy ["RNA-Seq"]', n_runs_measured 12, n_distinct_samples_measured 12, assay_probe_matched_text 'TempO-Seq'. research/literature/emc-fourth-cohort-publication-2026-08-24.json names the deposit's publication: PMID 42465974, doi 10.7717/peerj.21497, 'Prognostic biomarkers for enhanced risk stratification in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma: a retrospective cohort study', abstract 'We performed whole-transcriptome targeted RNA sequencing (TempO-Seq) on archiv[ed FFPE]', n = 12 FFPE, 6/6 prognosis split, with a whole characterisation manuscript at research/manuscripts/fusion-output/emc-fourth-cohort-sra-2026-08-08.md. systems/graph/blockers.json adds 'downloadable since 2025-11-11, carrying per-sample EWSR1 break-apart FISH status' — i.e. the fusion annotation §6.3 calls unknown is recorded as present. On the second half: the ATR document's own artifact (emc-atr-vulnerability.json → part_b.dataset_search.sra.studies) records SRP445369's name verbatim as 'Whole Genome Sequencing for Metastatic Mutational Burden in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma'. Consequences for the sentence as written: 'alignment and quantification from FASTQ' is the wrong pipeline for a TempO-Seq probe deposit (the repo's own emc_fourth_cohort_quant.py does probe-count matching, not transcriptome alignment), and the ATR document names neither PRJNA1357027 nor PMID 42465974, so a reader cannot cross-walk to the characterisation that already exists.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace the §6.3 row's 'the sample sizes and fusion annotation are unknown until it is opened' with the measured state and a pointer — n = 12 runs over 12 samples, whole-transcriptome targeted TempO-Seq (Chaiboonchoe et al., PeerJ 2026, PMID 42465974, doi 10.7717/peerj.21497), BioProject PRJNA1357027, characterised in emc-fourth-cohort-sra-2026-08-08.md — and drop SRP445369 from a row headed 'EMC RNA-seq quantified from raw reads' or relabel it as the whole-genome deposit it is. Any edit that keeps 'unknown' while this repository holds emc-sra-study.json restates a claim its own committed record falsifies.

p1s.summary: The Bangerter reference is printed with two different years in one document — §2.2 gives 'Hum Cell 2023;36:446-455', the Appendix gives 'Hum Cell 2022;36:446-455' — on the single sourced epidemiological bound (>90 % NR4A3 rearrangement) that stops §2.2 reading as a reclassification of a real cell line. Every fetched record in this repository, the document's own inputs cache included, says 2023.
p1s.evidence: At the pin, line 247-248 (§2.2): 'Bangerter et al., *Hum Cell* 2023;36:446-455, [PMID 36316541], [doi:10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x]'. Line 1028 (Appendix): 'Bangerter et al., *Hum Cell* 2022;36:446-455, [PMID 36316541]'. PubMed for 36316541 returns journal 'Human cell', volume 36, issue 1, pages 446-455, with publication_date 2022-11-01 (the Epub) — so volume 36 issue 1 is the 2023 print issue and 2023 is the citable year. The document's own emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json → part_a.literature records that PMID with year '2023'; research/literature/submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json records year 2023, volume 36, issue 1, pages 446-455, PMC9813045; two sibling manuscripts' reference lists (emc-fusion-partner-stratification.md [12], emc-surface-target-landscape.md) both write 2023. The '2022' matches only the DOI's own year segment (s13577-022-00818-x). The QUOTATION itself is exact against PubMed's abstract: 'EMCs are translocation sarcomas and harbor in > 90% of the cases an NR4A3 rearrangement.' This is the document's own recurring one-of-a-pair defect — the correction reached §2.2 and not its neighbour in the Appendix, which is the third instance the Appendix already records for other numbers.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Set both occurrences to 'Hum Cell 2023;36(1):446-455', matching every committed record. Any edit that leaves 2022 beside PMID 36316541 reintroduces the conflict with submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json and with the document's own inputs cache.

p2s.summary: The document's single most load-bearing identifier is invisible to the citation-provenance gate. PMID 34413129 is written only as 'PubMed=34413129' inside the Cellosaurus quotation, and none of lint_citations.py's three PMID patterns matches that spelling — so the identifier §2 rests on is outside the guard this repository built after the 2026-08-07 fabricated-PMID incident.
p2s.evidence: Calling the scanner directly on the quotation returns nothing for every kind: lint_citations.extract('PMID', '...(PubMed=34413129)."**') -> [], while extract('PMID', 'PMID 34413129') -> ['34413129']. The three patterns require the literal token 'PMID', a pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov URL, or 'EXT_ID:'; 'PubMed=' is Cellosaurus's own spelling and matches none. Nothing is wrong in fact — the identifier IS anchored in 15 tracked JSON files including the producing fetch cache, and citation-retraction-sweep.json records PMID:34413129 status 'clean' (PubMed esearch [uid], 2026-09-01) — and the full-repository run of lint_citations.py exits 0 with no line naming this file. The finding is that a green gate is not evidence here: the coverage of this particular identifier is luck, not measurement, which is this repository's standard failure shape.

p2s.summary: Four literature citations in §3.2 carry no identifier anywhere in the document and no fetch anchor anywhere in the repository — they are hard-coded string literals copied into the JSON, so the artifact anchors nothing. All four are correct, which I verified rather than assumed.
p2s.evidence: The document cites 'Milacic et al., *NAR* 2024' (Reactome), 'Ashburner et al., *Nat Genet* 2000' (GO), 'Liberzon et al., *Cell Syst* 2015' (MSigDB Hallmark) and 'Kuleshov et al., *NAR* 2016' (Enrichr) with no PMID or DOI. emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 187-197 hold these as literal Python strings, and emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#gene_sets._libraries_loaded[*].citation is the same string copied through — the exact self-anchoring hole lint_citations.py's own docstring documents. Verified against PubMed and all four are real and correctly attributed: Milacic M et al., 'The Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase 2024', Nucleic Acids Res 2024;52(D1):D672-D678, PMID 37941124, doi 10.1093/nar/gkad1025; Ashburner M et al., 'Gene ontology: tool for the unification of biology', Nat Genet 2000;25(1):25-9, PMID 10802651, doi 10.1038/75556; Liberzon A et al., 'The Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) hallmark gene set collection', Cell Syst 2015;1(6):417-425, PMID 26771021, doi 10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004; Kuleshov MV et al., 'Enrichr: a comprehensive gene set enrichment analysis web server 2016 update', Nucleic Acids Res 2016;44(W1):W90-7, PMID 27141961, doi 10.1093/nar/gkw377. Printing the four PMIDs would put them inside the gate at zero cost.

p2s.summary: Three compound-name mappings in §5 are typed rather than derived: the producing artifact carries only the GDSC codes, and the INN names appear in no fetch product in this repository. All three mappings are correct, which I verified rather than assumed.
p2s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d.gdsc_meta.drugs_with_data is exactly ['azd6738','bortezomib','mk-1775','olaparib','paclitaxel','talazoparib','ve-822'], and 'ceralasertib', 'berzosertib' and 'adavosertib' occur ZERO times in that artifact or in its inputs cache; a repository-wide grep finds them only in prose-derived review-seat records, method-watch-triggers.json and atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json. Verified live: PubMed's own query translation expands 'ceralasertib' to include 'azd6738'[All Fields] (an NLM Supplementary Concept synonym); berzosertib = VE-822 = VX-970 = M6620 (Selleck, MedChemExpress, and 'Phase 1 study of the ATR inhibitor berzosertib (formerly M6620, VX-970)', Br J Cancer, PMC8368196); adavosertib = MK-1775 = AZD1775, a WEE1 inhibitor (Selleck, MedChemExpress, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00648648 titled 'A Dose Escalation Study of Adavosertib (MK-1775)...'). The n values also check out exactly — azd6738 n_lines_with_residual 956 and ve-822 892, matching '956 lines with ceralasertib/AZD6738 and 892 with berzosertib/VE-822'. So the names are right; they are simply unanchored, and lint_citations has no pattern for a compound identifier.

p2s.summary: GSE299349's deposit date is stated two different ways in one document, and neither word matches the artifact's field name. §3.0a says 'deposited 2026-06-04'; §8.1 says 'submitted Jun 09 2025, released Jun 04 2026'. The parsed GEO record carries no release or status field at all.
p2s.evidence: atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json#series_record holds exactly two dates: submission_date 'Jun 09 2025' and last_update_date 'Jun 04 2026'. There is no 'status' or 'release' key in the parsed record, so 'released Jun 04 2026' converts last_update_date into a claim GEO's own record does not make (a series' last_update_date changes on any later metadata edit). Separately, §3.0a's 'deposited 2026-06-04' and §8.1's 'submitted Jun 09 2025' cannot both be true of one accession — one of the two sections calls the same deposit a year apart. Everything else in §8.1 verifies against the same record: title verbatim, overall_design verbatim, n_sample_ids_listed 68, platforms ['GPL24676','GPL34281'], pubmed_ids [] ('the series declares no PMID'), relations 'BioProject: .../PRJNA1273954', contributors 'Lara,,Planas-Paz' and 'Chantal,,Pauli' (which is also the exact provenance of the First,Middle,Last search bug the section reports).

p2s.summary: §8.2 says the published version turns the second quotation into 'a section heading and a figure caption rather than a running sentence' — implying a publisher change that did not happen. In the PREPRINT the same words are ALSO a Results section heading, not a running sentence.
p2s.evidence:
PMC10187251 (the version the document cites for this quotation): '...whether ES tumors are properly classified as BRCA-like cancers.

ES patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency.

We next directly examined genomic DNA from 100 ES patient tumor samples...' — the same paragraph-boundary-then-new-paragraph shape as its sibling headings 'EWSR1-FLI1 reduces resection-dependent DSB repair' and 'ATM activation and signaling is suppressed by the Ewing sarcoma fusion oncoprotein'. In PMC13223543 it appears as the heading 'Ewing sarcoma patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency' and as the Figure 2 caption. So the sentence's literal claim about the published version is TRUE, and its implied contrast is not: what the publisher changed is 'ES' to 'Ewing sarcoma', not the heading form. ⭐ The rest of §8.2's wording block verifies: EWSR1-FLI1 occurs 0 times and EWSR1::FLI1 135 times in the published text against 'Ewing sarcoma' 130 and ' ES ' 3, so 'throughout, ES becomes Ewing sarcoma and EWSR1-FLI1 becomes EWSR1::FLI1' is exact; the last quotation is genuinely split and reworded across a paragraph ('We find that Ewing sarcoma tumors are not "BRCA-like" (i.e., isolated loss of HR) but rather harbor partial ATM defects.' ... 'These data may explain the lack of clinical responses to PARP inhibitor monotherapy...'); and 'the substance is unchanged' holds on all four.
